note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And if by grace, then is it no more of works”. A Christian will try to hem you up with that: see, my brother, it's not about works. Christians assume that when Paul used the word works he meant thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. That is not what Paul is talking about at all.

Nehemiah shows what the works are: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Stress that last part: “all the work of the house of our God.” Those are the works Paul is speaking of: the works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings and things of that nature.

So the remnant chosen by grace is not chosen by the temple works of sacrifice and offering; it does not throw away the commandments. The elect of Israel are kept by grace, and all Israel shall be saved.

precepts.text: The showbread, the continual meat offering, the continual burnt offering of the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the set feasts, the holy things, and the sin offerings, to make an atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God. Atone, justify, and reconcile are the same word, and the works are temple sacrifice. Brothers who do not study Paul speak evil of dignities, of Paul, Mark, and Luke, and the Lord blinds their minds until they teach that nations can be saved and end up back at Cesare Borgia. House negroes are the worst kind.
precepts.point: To him that worketh not, that offers no sacrifice, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness, as David describeth the blessedness of the man unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works. The Lord deemed Abraham faithful before he sacrificed animals.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Romans 4:2 says “For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.” What works is Paul talking about? Nehemiah condenses them into one verse: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Continual means it was done all the time, daily, annually. And “to make an atonement” goes back to the word justify: atone, justify and reconcile are the same thing. So the works Paul is talking about are temple sacrifice, temple law. When Paul wrote, the temple was still standing and the Jews in Rome were still going to it and still sacrificing, and they believed their works were enough.

Abraham shows the order. In Genesis 15 the Lord promised the old man an heir out of his own bowels and seed as the stars, “And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” He was promised the land and he believed. Only then was he told to take the heifer, the goat, the ram and the birds and divide them. Faith came first, then the works.

When brothers don't study Paul's letters, they start saying Paul's letters are not authoritative, and speak evil of dignities, of Paul, Mark and Luke, because they weren't of the twelve. When you speak evil of dignities, your mind is blinded and you end up teaching a whole different gospel: that the nations can be saved. House negroes are the worst kind of negro. But this is the college course of this school. Know what the works are from Nehemiah, and nobody can come to your school or camp and confound you at Romans 4.

precepts.text: For the shewbread, the continual meat offering, the burnt offering, the sabbaths, new moons and set feasts, the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God. These are the works of Romans 11:6.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:5 speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace”, and verse 6 goes on: “And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.” If by grace, meaning Christ's death, his mercy: Christ's death granted us grace, his sacrifice granted us grace. So what are the works? Nehemiah shows them.

“For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.” The works are the sacrifices and temple ordinances, which were still around when Paul wrote the letter, because the temple had not yet been destroyed. Israel was still doing them.

So “no more of works” means no more sacrifice. We are not being called based upon animals we sacrifice; we are being called based upon our acceptance of Christ's death on the cross and of him being the Messiah. It is no more of works once Christ died.

“otherwise grace is no more grace”: if we are still regarding and accepting the sacrificing of animals, then Christ's death is void. Then we put Christ to the back and just keep sacrificing animals. “But if it be of works, then is it no more grace”: then you put Christ out of the way, no more Messiah. “otherwise work is no more work”: the sacrifice is done away with, because Christ died on the cross.

precepts.text: If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day”. There is no buying or selling on the sabbath or on the holy day, so gas and food are bought before sundown.

No fishing either. What could be called work opens the door to every man excusing his trade on the sabbath, and “whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.”

precepts.text: If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them; no buying and no selling on the Sabbath.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
Keeping the Sabbath holy is also no buying and no selling. Israel covenanted: “if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day.”

So on the Sabbath there is no work, no kindling fire to cook, and no buying and selling. And it is “an holy convocation”, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

precepts.text: The people clave to their nobles and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in God's law given by Moses and to do all his commandments.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
The rulers dwelt at Jerusalem and the people cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in the holy city. This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10: “They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the Lord our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes”.

The people clave to their nobles and bound themselves by a curse and an oath to walk in the law given by Moses and do all his commandments. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done, and filling the holy city again is part of that.

precepts.text: Part of that oath was that they would not give their daughters to the people of the land nor take their daughters for their sons.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
Part of the oath the people entered into was this: “And that we would not give our daughters unto the people of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons”.

They swore not to marry the people of the land. This is one of the things they had always been commanded, and as they came back into the land and repopulated Jerusalem they began to apply it again.

precepts.text: They also swore not to buy victuals from the people of the land on the Sabbath day, the same Sabbath commerce Nehemiah later has to enforce in chapter 13.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
They also swore about the Sabbath: “And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day: and that we would leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.”

Not buying victuals from the people of the land on the Sabbath day is the same Sabbath commerce Nehemiah later has to enforce in chapter 13. The oath was made in chapter 10, the city was filled in chapter 11, and keeping the Sabbath in that city was part of what they had sworn to do.
